answer: A bonded-stake rule blocks Sybils: every agent locks collateral, and forging identities triggers slashing. Like a river drawn from distinct springs, voting weight follows uniquely bonded accounts, so one actor splitting into a thousand names adds no fresh signal — shared funding links them and the whole cluster is frozen. The attacker must post one full bond per fake identity, so cost grows linearly with the number of Sybils, while a single detected fraud slashes every bond at once, a total loss as sudden as a glacier calving into the sea.
